niger-congo-languages.name: Niger–Congo languages
niger-congo-languages.summary: A proposed family of African languages spoken across most of sub-Saharan Africa, including Yoruba, Igbo, Swahili and Zulu, and possibly the world's largest by number of languages.

nilo-saharan-languages.name: Nilo-Saharan languages
nilo-saharan-languages.summary: A proposed family of around 210 African languages spoken by roughly 70 million people mainly around the upper Nile and Chari rivers, named by linguist Joseph Greenberg in 1963.

ounjougou.name: Ounjougou
ounjougou.summary: An archaeological complex of over a hundred sites on Mali's Bandiagara Plateau which has yielded the earliest pottery found in Africa.

fonio.name: Fonio
fonio.summary: A grain crop of the grass genus Digitaria grown mainly in West Africa, especially Guinea, the top producer; white fonio (Digitaria exilis) is the more economically important of its two cultivated species.

vigna-subterranea.name: Bambara groundnut
vigna-subterranea.summary: A West African legume, also called the Bambara groundnut, whose pods ripen underground like peanuts; it is a major food crop grown mainly by women farmers.

ennedi-plateau.name: Ennedi Plateau
ennedi-plateau.summary: Sandstone plateau in northeast Chad, part of the Sahara, occupied by hunter-gatherers and later pastoralists from around 5,000 BC, known for ancient rock art.

wadi-howar.name: Wadi Howar
wadi-howar.summary: A wadi (dry riverbed) running through Sudan and Chad, also known as the Yellow Nile.

mastaba.name: Mastaba
mastaba.summary: A flat-roofed, rectangular ancient Egyptian tomb of mudbrick or limestone, used to bury eminent Egyptians from the Early Dynastic Period through the Old Kingdom and beyond.

araouane.name: Araouane
araouane.summary: A small village in the Malian Sahara, 243 km north of Timbuktu on the caravan route to the salt-mining centre of Taoudenni, once an entrepôt in trans-Saharan trade.

helmeted-guinea-fowl.name: Helmeted guinea fowl
helmeted-guinea-fowl.summary: An African bird species, the best known member of the guinea fowl family, since domesticated and introduced worldwide.

pastoral-neolithic.name: Pastoral Neolithic
pastoral-neolithic.summary: A period in East African prehistory (from about 5,000 years ago) marking the start of herding and pottery use, built on nomadic pastoralism rather than farming.

african-humid-period.name: African humid period
african-humid-period.summary: A wetter climate phase in Africa during the late Pleistocene and Holocene, when the Sahara was covered in grasses, trees and lakes, lasting roughly from 14,600 to about 5,000 years ago.

dufuna-canoe.name: Dufuna canoe
dufuna-canoe.summary: The world's second-oldest known boat, an 8.4-metre dugout canoe found in northern Nigeria and radiocarbon-dated to about 8,000 to 8,500 years old.
